national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that the surgical strike by the Indian Army on the terrorist hideouts in Pakistan demonstrated a new example of India’s counter-terrorism policy to the world. Addressing the nation in his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani, Mr Modi said India is set to mark the tenth anniversary of the surgical strike tomorrow (28th September). He said the world was astonished to see the manner in which brave Indian soldiers crossed the Line of Control to take action against terrorism. Prime Minister Modi said the surgical strike was India’s decisive response to the long-standing pain the nation had endured due to terrorist attacks. He stated that over the past decade – from the Balakot airstrike to ‘Operation Sindoor ’, India has repeatedly sent the message that terrorist strikes will be met with a befitting response. Mr Modi recounted that there was a time when serial blasts had become a common occurrence in the country. He said many lives were lost in the serial blasts in Delhi on 13th September, 2008. The 26/11 attack took place just a few weeks later in Mumbai. He highlighted that today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and country is witnessing the results of that. Prime Minister Modi said this year also marks 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks. He said that the highest number of victims at the World Trade Center in the US, after Americans, were Indians. He recalled paying homage to those innocent citizens during his US visit after becoming Prime Minister in 2014. He once again extended his condolences to the bereaved families on behalf of crores of Indian citizens. Touching upon the topic of the ongoing census, Mr Modi said the first phase of this exercise is nearly complete across all States and Union Territories. Data of over 32 crore families has already been recorded. Work is currently underway also in the remote, snow-clad regions of Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttarakhand. The Prime Minister noted that many inspiring experiences have emerged from these areas. In Uttarakhand, the census process began in the village of Mana in Chamoli, which is known as the country’s first village. Prime Minister Modi said the process there started with 83-year-old Purnima Rawat. In Bagori village of Uttarkashi, Hardev Singh Rana, who runs a homestay, entered his details himself using digital means. Mr Modi emphasised that the census is a national responsibility for all. He added that the facility to self-register census details is very convenient and people can register information about themselves and their family from their mobiles. Along with Hindi, this facility is available in 16 languages. The Prime Minister asked people to visit the census online portal, se.census.gov.in, and log in with their mobile number, enter location, fill in details regarding their family and submit the information. The Prime Minister said the entire process takes about 15 to 20 minutes. No document needs to be uploaded for this. After submitting the information, people will receive a special ID, which can be shared with the census enumerator when they pay a visit. After the information is verified, it becomes part of the census record. Prime Minister Modi informed that so far, more than 2 crore 60 lakh people have already entered their details on the census portal via mobile, completing the self-enumeration. He said accurate information about citizens and their families helps create a precise picture of the country’s future. The Prime Minister said today marks the 100th birth anniversary of the revered late Ashok Singhal, who was the former International Working President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad. He called him a great personality who dedicated his entire life to culture, society, and the nation. Born on 27th September, 1926, in Agra, Ashok Singhal led a life as an ascetic even though living amidst society. Prime Minister Modi said the very direction and energy he imparted to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement veritably resulted in the magnificent temple in Ayodhya today. Alongside the Ram Mandir movement, Ashok Singhal also waged a major battle against social discrimination and inequality. Mr Modi offered his tributes on the occasion of his birth centenary. national_raw_news.content: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh today said that India is building capabilities keeping in mind the nature of warfare over the next 10, 20 and 25 years, as it moves towards creating a self-reliant and future-orientated defence ecosystem. He made these remarks while speaking at an event organised by a media house in New Delhi. Mr Singh emphasised that the country should not merely focus on importing technology but should strive to define and develop defence technologies. The Minister said that in the future, the security domain and the battlefield will be technology-driven, and countries that lead in technology will have an advantage on the battlefield. He said this is why India is focusing on making its defence strategy future-ready, with the emphasis not only on developing weapons for today but also on preparing for future challenges. Mr Singh stressed that modern warfare is no longer limited to armed forces or weapons but has become multi-sectoral. Highlighting the growth of the defence sector, he said that over the past 12 years, the country’s defence capabilities have increased significantly, along with a major change in its approach towards strengthening national security. The Minister said that the government has also substantially increased capital allocation in the defence budget. He highlighted that nearly 75 percent of the capital acquisition budget of one lakh 39 thousand crore rupees has been earmarked for procurement from the domestic defence industry. Mr Singh said that to promote self-reliance in defence, the armed forces have issued five Positive Indigenisation Lists, covering a total of 509 defence equipment, weapon systems and platforms. Mr Singh iterated that India believes in peace and does not want war. He said India neither wants to occupy the territory of any country nor intimidate any country. He emphasised that there is a difference between peace and weakness. He said India wants peace but will not compromise on its security.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | Sports 195 India to face West Indies in first ODI in Thiruvananthapuram today
national_raw_news.content: In Men’s Cricket, the first One Day International of the 3-match series between India and West Indies will be played today at the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram. The match will start at 2 PM IST. Both Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli return to India’s ODI lineup after a two-month break from this format. Shubman Gill will lead Team India for this ODI series, while Shai Hope captains the West Indies. Akashvani correspondent reports the enthusiasm among cricket fans, which surged from the opening of ticket sales, has reached its peak with the arrival of both teams in Thiruvananthapuram. Cricket fans in the city are hoping to see India make a strong start in the opening match of the three-match ODI series. Tight security arrangements have been put in place at Thiruvananthapuram in connection with the India-West Indies match. Smithy M Palluruthy, Akashavani News, Thiruvananthapuram.” The second ODI will be played in Guwahati on September 30, followed by the third One Day International in New Chandigarh on October 3. The ODI series will be followed by five T20 internationals. Shreyas Iyer will lead the team in the T20I series. The T20 international series will begin in Lucknow on October 6, followed by the second T20I in Ranchi on October 9, the third in Indore on October 11, the fourth in Hyderabad on October 14, and the fifth in Bengaluru on October 17.

national_raw_news.title: Country’s first world-class geological museum to be developed in Madhya Pradesh 1 hour ago 33
national_raw_news.content: A world-class geological museum, the first of its kind in the country will be developed at the famous Bhedaghat-Lamhetaghat area in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. The Central Government has approved a project worth 87 crore rupees for this. The project will be developed on around 12 hectares of land under the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme. A geological museum and interpretation centre will be built under the project. It will have six galleries and more than 130 exhibits. Other attractions will include 3D models, interactive touch tables, digital panels, an immersive theatre, Titanosaur Square, dinosaur park, fossil garden, geological maze, rock garden, tree-top walkway, glass floor, nature walks and viewing decks. The museum will explain the origin of the Earth and the geological history of the Narmada Valley and Madhya Pradesh, going back millions of years, in a simple and interesting way. The project will focus on protecting the natural surroundings and existing trees. The aim is to keep 90 per cent or more of the area green. Restaurants, food courts, shops selling local products and an eco-resort will also be developed. The project is targeted for completion by February 2028, within 18 months. The Madhya Pradesh Tourism Board will implement the project.

national_raw_news.title: Flood situation worsens in Odisha following continuous heavy rainfall 4 hours ago 105
national_raw_news.content: The flood situation is worsening in several parts of Odisha following heavy rainfall over the past few days, with rivers swelling and low-lying areas inundated. The Jalaka is flowing above the danger level, while the Subarnarekha is rising rapidly, raising concern in northern Odisha. In the Mahanadi basin, heavy rainfall in the upper catchments of Chhattisgarh has increased inflows into Hirakud reservoir, prompting release of excess water through its gates. Akashvani correspondent reports that rainfall continues in several parts of Odisha, aggravating the flood situation in the state. The Jalaka river is flowing above the danger level at Mathani in Balasore district, while the Subarnarekha is also rising and remains close to the danger mark at Rajghat. Several low-lying areas have been inundated. In the Mahanadi basin, heavy rainfall in the upper catchments of Chhattisgarh has led to increased inflow into the Hirakud reservoir. Twenty-two gates of Hirakud Dam are currently open for release of excess water. People living in low-lying areas along the Mahanadi and its tributaries have been advised to remain alert. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast further heavy to very heavy rainfall at some places in Odisha, and authorities are closely monitoring the flood situation.
